brief.outcome: Bring cost per booked job from an estimated $150 to under $90 within three months, without booking fewer jobs than now, by judging Google Ads on booked jobs instead of leads.

ambition.goal_beyond: Every ad dollar is judged by booked jobs and what they earn, so spend can later be raised with confidence instead of by guesswork
rungs: Cut wasted clicks and cheap junk leads so the $50 lead gets cheaper
Count booked jobs by ad source from Housecall Pro, find where leads are lost (junk leads, missed calls on the shared phone, wasted search terms) and fix the biggest cause
Keep it true: send booked jobs back to Google Ads and run a weekly cost per booked job check that flags drift
ambition.judge: Housecall Pro booked jobs for the same weeks, matched to Google Ads spend by the lead source label, read against the baseline of about 40 booked jobs a month once it is counted

brief.deliverable: A checked count of booked jobs by Google Ads source, a diagnosis of where the $6,000 is lost, a ready call-handling and conversion set-up, account changes applied live with the owner's approval, and a weekly readout of cost per booked job

answers.question: The business
answers.answer: Plumbing company with six vans in Austin, Texas

answers.question: Spend and leads now
answers.answer: $6,000 a month on Google Ads, about 120 leads at $50 each (Google Ads dashboard)

answers.question: Booked jobs
answers.answer: Thinks only a third of leads become booked jobs, but this is not tracked properly

answers.question: Phones and booking
answers.answer: Calls go to a shared phone; Housecall Pro is used for bookings

answers.question: Tools and access
answers.answer: Google Ads MCP connected with live access; Housecall Pro exports only

answers.question: Target
answers.answer: Cost per booked job under $90 within three months, with booked jobs at least as high as now

answers.question: Limits
answers.answer: No changes to the service area

research.approach: Practitioners in home services stop judging Google Ads by cost per lead, because a lead can be a two-second call, a wrong number or a job-seeker. They count booked jobs, and revenue per job where possible, by ad source, and send those outcomes back to Google so bidding aims at jobs. Before any change they check what the account counts as a lead (call length, duplicates, forms), then read 90 days of search terms, hours, locations and job types against booked jobs. For a business with one shared phone, call handling is part of the ad cost, because a missed call is a paid click wasted. Changes go in small groups, one at a time and logged, so the effect of each can be read.

steps.name: Rebuild 90 days of spend, leads and Housecall Pro jobs side by side
steps.why: $50 per lead and one booked job in three are reports until the raw rows reproduce them.

steps.name: Check what Google Ads counts as a lead and how many are real
steps.why: Short calls, duplicates and wrong-service calls make the lead cost look better than the job cost.

steps.name: Match leads to booked jobs and measure the true booked share
steps.why: Cost per booked job needs the booked share, which the owner says is not tracked.

steps.name: Read search terms, hours, locations and job types against booked jobs
steps.why: Waste hides in terms and hours that bring calls but not jobs.

steps.name: Check call handling on the shared phone
steps.why: A missed or badly handled call wastes the click that paid for it.

steps.name: Send booked jobs back to Google Ads and set bidding on them
steps.why: Bidding on booked jobs stops it paying for cheap calls that never book.

steps.name: Apply changes in small logged groups, with a comparison
steps.why: One group at a time shows which change moved cost per booked job.

steps.name: Read cost per booked job weekly against the baseline
steps.why: Weekly reading catches drift and keeps the guardrail on booked jobs.

steps.name: Move part of the budget to Local Services Ads
steps.why: Pay-per-lead ads with a Google Guaranteed badge are a common channel for plumbers.

pitfalls.text: Cutting the lead cost by counting more calls as leads, while booked jobs do not change.
Adding negative keywords for terms with no conversions without checking they were really unwanted demand, which can cut booked jobs.
Switching bidding to booked jobs before enough jobs have been imported to learn from.
Judging the shared phone by leads when the real loss is missed calls and slow call-backs.
Changing many things in one week so no change can be credited or blamed.
Matching jobs to ad clicks with customer phone numbers kept in the open sheet instead of hashed.

stages.name: Pin down the goal
stages.goal: Turn the request into a measured goal, limits and the data we can reach. Writes BRIEF.md.

stages.name: Rebuild spend, leads and jobs
stages.goal: Pull 90 days of Google Ads results, call details and Housecall Pro jobs into the Google Sheet, side by side by week.

checks.name: Spend and lead totals match the Google Ads dashboard within 2% for the same dates, and the lead total is within 5 of the reported 120 a month
Housecall Pro rows cover the same 90 days with a source label on every row or the share without one is stated
Customer phone numbers are hashed or removed in the sheet
Missing data is named with what it blocks

stages.name: Check what a lead is and match leads to jobs
stages.goal: Check what Google Ads counts as a lead, remove duplicates, match leads to Housecall Pro jobs and measure the true booked share and cost per booked job.

checks.name: Every conversion action counted as a lead is listed with its rule (for example call length) and whether it is a primary goal
The share of counted calls under 60 seconds is stated
The share of leads matched to a Housecall Pro job is stated, and the booked share is computed with its method, or marked LIMITED
Ends with CHECKED, LIMITED or UNRELIABLE and the cost per booked job it supports

stages.name: Find where the $6,000 is lost
stages.goal: Test the hypotheses on junk leads, wasted terms, call handling, hours, job types and locations, and keep competing explanations.

checks.name: Every hypothesis is SUPPORTED, REFUTED or UNKNOWN, with the numbers used
A segment finding needs at least 30 clicks or 10 leads, otherwise it is marked low-confidence
Cost per booked job is spend divided by jobs for the whole segment, not an average of averages
Each main finding names a competing explanation

stages.name: Rank what to change
stages.goal: Turn supported findings into ranked options with expected effect on cost per booked job and on booked jobs, effort, confidence, risk and measurement, and set the spend limit per booked job.

checks.name: Every option cites the finding it rests on
Every option has expected effect on cost per booked job and on booked jobs, effort, confidence, risk and how it is measured
Measurement fixes rank first when the lead check is not CHECKED
No option changes the service area

stages.name: Owner chooses
stages.goal: The owner picks the options. Ask for the reason when the top option is passed over and record it.

checks.name: Chosen and passed-over options are in decisions.jsonl
A reason is recorded wherever the top option was passed over

stages.name: Prepare booked-job tracking and call handling
stages.goal: Prepare the lead source labels for Housecall Pro, the weekly booked-jobs file for Google Ads, the conversion goal change, and a short call-handling routine for the shared phone.

checks.name: Only chosen changes are included
The upload file carries the click ID or hashed customer details only, never plain phone numbers or names
Each step says how to confirm it worked, such as a test job appearing as a conversion in Google Ads
The call routine sets who answers, a call-back time and a source label on every ad lead

stages.name: Prepare the account changes
stages.goal: Prepare the chosen Google Ads changes as an exact list in groups: negative keywords with level and match type, hours, ad copy that qualifies the caller, and bidding.

checks.name: Only chosen changes are included, grouped so each group can be applied and read on its own
Each negative keyword has a level, a match type and the search term rows that justify it
Location settings are left exactly as they are
Each group says how to undo it

stages.name: Apply changes in logged groups
stages.goal: Apply the measurement changes first, then one group of account changes at a time, each approved by the owner and logged, with the comparison registered before the first change.

checks.name: The comparison (weekly cost per booked job and booked jobs, with the weeks before as baseline) is registered in experiments.jsonl before the first change
Tracking goes first and bidding on booked jobs is switched only after at least 30 booked jobs are imported, otherwise the current bidding stays
Each applied group was read back from the account and matches the change list
Daily budgets are unchanged and the monthly total stays at or below $6,000

stages.name: Read cost per booked job weekly
stages.goal: Each week, read spend, leads, booked jobs and cost per booked job from Housecall Pro against the baseline, and check every guardrail.

checks.name: Booked jobs come from Housecall Pro rows, not from Google Ads conversions alone
Booked jobs per month are compared with the baseline and flagged if lower by more than 10%
A verdict on cost per booked job needs at least 30 booked jobs in the period, otherwise INCONCLUSIVE
Compared weeks have the same weekday mix and the same attribution

stages.name: Keep what we learned
stages.goal: Close the comparison, record which changes moved cost per booked job, propose rules with their scope, and decide whether Local Services Ads deserve a test.

checks.name: The registered comparison is closed in experiments.jsonl with a verdict
Each proposed rule says whether it holds for this account, this business or any plumber

hypotheses.statement: A large share of the 120 counted leads are not real jobs (very short calls, wrong service, job-seekers, duplicates).
hypotheses.test: Call details and conversion actions: share of counted calls under 60 seconds, calls from outside the service area, and duplicate conversions.
hypotheses.confirm_if: More than 25% of counted leads are under 60 seconds, outside the area, or duplicates.

hypotheses.statement: The true booked share is not about a third, so the real cost per booked job differs from $150.
hypotheses.test: Match leads to Housecall Pro jobs by week and compute booked jobs divided by leads.
hypotheses.confirm_if: The matched booked share is below 25% or above 45%.

hypotheses.statement: A fifth of the spend goes to search terms that never produce a booked job.
hypotheses.test: Spend by search term against matched booked jobs over 90 days, for terms with at least 30 clicks.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Terms with no booked job and at least 30 clicks take 20% or more of spend.
hypotheses.refute_if: Such terms take less than 10% of spend.

hypotheses.statement: Calls from ads are lost on the shared phone (missed, slow call-back, no booking attempt).
hypotheses.test: Two-week phone tally: answered share, median call-back time, and booked share of answered calls.
hypotheses.confirm_if: More than 20% of ad calls are missed, or fewer than half of answered calls end in a booking or quote.
hypotheses.refute_if: Fewer than 10% are missed and most answered calls end in a booking or quote.

hypotheses.statement: Spend in hours when nobody answers or when calls rarely book is wasted.
hypotheses.test: Spend, calls and booked jobs by hour of day and weekday, with the phone tally.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Hours with at least 15% of spend have a cost per booked job over 1.5 times the average, or an answered share under 50%.
hypotheses.refute_if: Cost per booked job is within 20% of the average across hours.

hypotheses.statement: Cheap or low-value job types soak up spend while higher-value jobs are under-served.
hypotheses.test: Cost per booked job and invoice value by job type for types with at least 10 jobs.
hypotheses.confirm_if: The cheapest type to win costs less than half the dearest per booked job, or revenue per ad dollar differs by 2 times or more.
hypotheses.refute_if: Types are within 25% on both measures.

hypotheses.statement: Bidding is optimising for cheap calls, not booked jobs.
hypotheses.test: Read the conversion goals and bid strategy for each campaign.
hypotheses.confirm_if: All calls count as a primary conversion and a conversions-based strategy is on, with no booked-job signal.
hypotheses.refute_if: Bidding already uses booked jobs or call quality.

hypotheses.statement: Costs rose because clicks got dearer, not because the ads got worse.
hypotheses.test: Cost per click and conversion rate by month over the last 6 months.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Cost per click rose 20% or more while conversion rate stayed within 10%.
hypotheses.refute_if: Cost per click is flat and the change is in conversion rate.

dropped.reason: Local Services Ads are a separate account with a screening step and are not in the connected Google Ads MCP; the owner can decide at the learning stage once booked-job costs are known.

measurement.window: Weekly readout, with the baseline taken from the 90 days before the first change and a verdict after 12 weeks.
measurement.min_volume: At least 30 booked jobs in the period read, and at least 30 clicks or 10 leads for any segment finding.
measurement.stop_rule: Undo the last group of changes if booked jobs fall more than 10% below the baseline for 2 weeks in a row, or if calls from ads are no longer being answered; otherwise run the full window before a verdict.
